patients.summary: Healthy mechanical engineering graduate student who joined in September 2024. Two high-speed car crashes a year apart: a duodenal rupture repaired at laparotomy in January 2025, and a liver laceration with hemoperitoneum controlled at repeat laparotomy with transfusion in January 2026. Recovered fully from both; nothing open today.

social.value: Occasional social use, 1-2 drinks per month

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
24 y/o man here to get a doctor in the area. Started a PhD program in mechanical engineering this fall and moved to the area for it, renting in Leeds. Had a pediatrician and then a primary care office back home; records release signed today.

No medical problems that he knows of. No surgeries, no hospital stays. Takes nothing, not even supplements. NKDA.
FH: nothing he's aware of on either side.
SH: never smoked, no vaping. Alcohol maybe a drink or two a month, at a department thing or out with friends. No drugs. Single.

ROS negative across the board. Sleep is fine apart from deadlines.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well, relaxed. HEENT unremarkable, TMs clear, oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no adenopathy. Heart regular rate, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, non-tender, no masses or organomegaly. Skin clear. Neuro grossly normal.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P
Healthy young adult, establishing care.
- Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids. One-time HIV and hep C screen, he's fine with both.
- Vaccines: will check what the prior office sends. Flu and COVID once this season's doses are in, likely October.
- Gave him the practice cell; text for anything.
Return yearly or as needed.

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Records received by fax from patient's previous primary care office, 22 pages, scanned to chart.

Summary for the PCP: well visits from adolescence through 2023, no chronic problems, no surgeries, no prescriptions on file. Allergies: none listed. Childhood series documented complete; HPV and meningococcal series complete; Tdap given 08/2018 before college. Last visit 06/2023 was a sports-physical type check, normal.

Tdap entered in immunization history.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mehmet, all of Tuesday's bloodwork looks normal: blood counts, kidney and liver numbers, sugar and cholesterol are all fine, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens came back negative. Nothing to follow up on. We'll put flu and COVID shots on the calendar once the fall supply arrives.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Came in after classes for vaccines. No fever or illness today, no prior vaccine reactions, NKDA.
Influenza vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid.
COVID-19 mRNA (2024-25 formula) 0.3 mL IM right deltoid.
VIS given for both. Waited 15 min in the lobby without issue. Told him a sore arm or feeling run down for a day is common.

events.reason: Abdominal pain after high-speed motor vehicle collision

reports.text:
UPRIGHT AP CHEST, SINGLE VIEW
Indication: high-speed motor vehicle collision, upper abdominal pain.
Comparison: none.
Findings: Lungs are clear. No pneumothorax or pleural effusion. Heart and mediastinum are normal in size and contour. No rib fracture identified. A small amount of free air is present beneath the diaphragm.
reports.conclusion: Small volume of free air under the diaphragm. No rib fracture. Findings communicated to the ED physician at the time of reading.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST
Indication: blunt abdominal trauma, free air on chest film.
Technique: axial images from the lung bases through the pelvis after IV contrast, with multiplanar reformats.
Findings: Free air is present in the retroperitoneum adjacent to the pancreas. The liver, spleen, adrenal glands and kidneys are intact without laceration or contusion. The pancreas enhances normally. No free intraperitoneal fluid. Bowel is otherwise unremarkable. Bladder normal. No fracture of the visualized spine, ribs or pelvis.
reports.conclusion: Retroperitoneal free air adjacent to the pancreas, consistent with duodenal injury in this setting. Solid organs intact. Discussed with the trauma surgery team.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 01/11/2025
Received by fax 01/20/2025.

CC: upper abdominal pain after car crash.

HPI: 25 y/o M brought by ambulance. He was driving, belted, when his car went off the road at speed and struck a tree. Complains of a dull, mild-to-moderate ache across the upper abdomen. No nausea or vomiting, bowel habits unchanged. No neck pain.

PMH: none. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
SH: graduate student. Never smoker, rare alcohol, none today.
FH: noncontributory.

Exam: Alert, uncomfortable but conversant. Vitals stable throughout ED course (see flowsheet). No ecchymosis, abrasion or seatbelt mark on chest or abdomen. Epigastrium mildly tender to palpation; no rebound, no guarding. Bowel sounds present and normal. Chest wall non-tender. Pelvis stable. Neuro intact.

ED course: Labs drawn: Hgb 13.8, WBC 12.0, amylase 90, lipase 45. Upright chest film read with a small amount of subdiaphragmatic free air and no rib fractures. CT abdomen/pelvis then showed retroperitoneal free air next to the pancreas. Trauma surgery at bedside; NPO, IV fluids, IV antibiotics started.

Impression: blunt abdominal trauma with duodenal rupture.
Disposition: admitted to trauma surgery for the operating room.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain. Dispense #20.
Take 2 tablets by mouth every 8 hours

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of operation: 01/11/2025
Received by fax 01/20/2025.

Preoperative diagnosis: blunt duodenal injury (retroperitoneal free air on CT).
Postoperative diagnosis: traumatic duodenal perforation.
Procedure: exploratory laparotomy, primary repair of duodenal perforation, placement of closed suction drain.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal.
Allergies: NKDA.
EBL: minimal. Specimens: none. Complications: none.

Findings and technique: Midline laparotomy. A small amount of bilious staining in the retroperitoneum. Kocher maneuver performed and the duodenum mobilized; a full-thickness perforation was identified, edges healthy. Debrided minimally and closed primarily in two layers, transversely. Liver, spleen, stomach, small bowel and colon inspected and intact. No hemoperitoneum. Closed suction drain left adjacent to the repair. Fascia closed with running suture, skin with staples. NG tube in good position. Patient to the surgical floor in stable condition.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — TRAUMA SURGERY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 01/11/2025, discharged 01/16/2025.
Received by fax 01/20/2025.

Diagnosis: traumatic duodenal perforation after high-speed MVC (restrained driver).
Procedure: exploratory laparotomy with primary duodenal repair, 01/11/2025.
Allergies: NKDA.

Hospital course: Taken to the OR from the ED the evening of arrival. Postoperatively kept NPO with NG decompression; piperacillin-tazobactam given for 24 hours perioperatively. NG out on POD 2. Bowel function returned, drain output low and non-bilious, so the drain was pulled and diet advanced on POD 4, which he tolerated. Ambulating independently. Pain controlled on oral medication. Uncomplicated course.

Discharge medications:
- Oxycodone 5 mg, 1 tab every 6 hours as needed for pain, #20
- Acetaminophen 1000 mg every 8 hours

Instructions: no lifting more than 10 lb for 6 weeks from surgery. No driving while taking oxycodone. Staples to come out at trauma clinic in about 2 weeks. Return for fever, worsening pain, vomiting, or redness or drainage from the incision.
Follow-up: trauma surgery clinic 01/28/2025; primary care within one week.

documents.title: Patient Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Mehmet called the practice cell from his hospital bed. Crashed his car Saturday afternoon, had abdominal surgery that night for a tear in the duodenum. Says the team tells him things are going well, NG tube came out today or will soon, he isn't sure. Pain manageable. Wanted us to know.
Told him we'll request the ED and operative records and see him within a week of discharge. Front desk to send records request to the hospital and to reach out to schedule once he knows his discharge date.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge visit. Hospital records reviewed (ED note, CT, op note, d/c summary from 1/11-1/16). Restrained driver in a single-car crash into a tree, retroperitoneal free air on CT, duodenal perforation repaired primarily at laparotomy the same night. Uneventful stay.

Home since Thursday. Got a ride here today. Pain is down to a 3 most of the day, worse getting out of bed. Taking the oxycodone once, sometimes twice a day, and acetaminophen on schedule. Eating regular meals, smaller portions. Bowels moving. No fever, no vomiting. Not driving.

Exam: vitals as charted. Comfortable sitting, a little slow getting onto the table. Midline incision with staples intact, edges well approximated, no redness, no drainage. Old drain site dry with a dressing. Abdomen otherwise soft, appropriately tender near the wound.

A/P
S/p ex lap and primary repair of traumatic duodenal perforation 1/11/25, recovering as expected.
- Taper oxycodone off over the next several days; keep acetaminophen. Disposal bag given for leftover tabs.
- Keep 1/28 trauma clinic appointment for staple removal.
- 10 lb lifting limit until about 2/22, per surgery.
- Text if fever, wound changes, worsening pain.

documents.title: Trauma Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

I saw Mr. Saleh in trauma clinic on 01/28/2025, 17 days after exploratory laparotomy and primary repair of a traumatic duodenal perforation.

He is doing well. Off oxycodone since the weekend, using acetaminophen now and then. Tolerating a regular diet, normal bowel function, no fevers. Allergies: NKDA.

The midline incision is healing nicely; staples were removed and Steri-Strips applied. Drain site closed. Abdomen soft and appropriately tender.

He should keep to the 10 lb lifting limit until six weeks from surgery, then advance as tolerated. I will see him again in about six weeks.

Sincerely,
Trauma Surgery

documents.title: Back to the lab?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, quick question. My advisor wants me back running the test rig, which means moving fixtures that are probably 25-30 lb. Also I'd like to get back to the gym. Is it ok yet? Surgery was Jan 11. Incision looks fine.

documents.title: RE: Back to the lab?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good to hear the incision looks fine. The surgeons asked for no more than 10 lb for six weeks, so that runs through about Feb 22. Lab work that doesn't involve lifting is fine now; have someone else move the fixtures until then, and after that build back up gradually over a couple of weeks. Same for the gym: walking, bike or elliptical now, weights after the 22nd starting light. Your trauma clinic visit in March will give you the final word. Happy to write a note for your advisor if that helps.

documents.title: Trauma Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

Mr. Saleh returned to trauma clinic on 03/11/2025, two months after repair of his duodenal perforation. He has no complaints. Eating normally, bowels regular, back at work in his lab and gradually returning to exercise. NKDA.

On exam the incision is fully healed without hernia. Abdomen soft and non-tender.

He has recovered from his injury and is cleared for full activity without restriction. No routine follow-up is needed with us; we would be glad to see him again for any concerns.

Sincerely,
Trauma Surgery

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Here for seasonal shots. Feels well, no reactions last year beyond a sore arm.
Flu 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. COVID-19 mRNA 2025-26, 0.5 mL IM L deltoid.
VIS sheets reviewed. Observed 15 minutes, left feeling fine. Reminded him his physical is due around December.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. 26 now. Second year of the PhD, qualifying exam behind him. Feels well.

Interval: ex lap with primary repair of a traumatic duodenal perforation in Jan after a car crash; trauma clinic released him in March. No abdominal symptoms since. Eats whatever he wants, bowels normal. Back to the gym.
Meds: none. NKDA.
SH: never smoker, a drink or two a month. No drugs.
FH: noncontributory.

ROS negative.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well-appearing. HEENT normal. Neck without nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen: well-healed midline scar, no hernia with cough, soft, non-tender, no organomegaly. Skin otherwise clear. Neuro normal.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P
Well adult.
- History of duodenal repair, fully recovered. Nothing further needed.
- CBC and CMP today.
- Flu and COVID done in October. Tdap 2018, next due 2028.
- Seatbelt every time; he says he has been extra careful since the crash.
See in a year.

documents.title: Results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mehmet, your labs from yesterday are all normal. Blood count is solid (hemoglobin 14.2), and kidney, liver and sugar values are fine. See you next December, or sooner if anything comes up. Good luck finishing the semester.

documents.title: Trauma Resuscitation Record
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL TRAUMA CENTER — TRAUMA BAY / ICU ADMISSION NOTE
Date of service: 01/14/2026
Received by fax 01/21/2026.

CC: low blood pressure and pallor after a high-speed crash.

HPI: 26 y/o M, belted driver in a high-speed collision with airbag deployment, brought in as a trauma activation. Awake and answering questions on arrival, visibly pale and anxious. Initial BP 90/60 with HR 120; despite rapid crystalloid boluses the pressure drifted to 85/55. Complains of right upper abdominal pain.

PMH: blunt abdominal trauma in a separate car crash 01/2025, treated with laparotomy and repair of a duodenal perforation, recovered.
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
SH: graduate student, never smoker, social alcohol only.
FH: noncontributory.

Primary survey: airway intact, breath sounds equal, SpO2 97% on room air, RR 22. Circulation as above, two large-bore IVs.
Abdomen: distended; tender in the RUQ with guarding; no rebound; bowel sounds normal; healed midline scar.

Labs: Hgb 9.8 (14.2 at his PCP's office one month ago), Hct 29.4, platelets 250. LFTs within normal limits. Coags normal.
FAST: free fluid in the hepatorenal recess (Morison's pouch).

Assessment: hemoperitoneum from liver injury, hypotensive and not responding to fluid.
Plan: uncrossmatched blood started, straight to the OR for laparotomy. ICU afterward.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain. Dispense #15.
Take 2 tablets by mouth every 8 hours

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL TRAUMA CENTER — OPERATIVE REPORT
Date: 01/14/2026
Received by fax 01/21/2026.

Preop diagnosis: hemoperitoneum, hemodynamic instability after blunt trauma, FAST positive.
Postop diagnosis: liver laceration with hemoperitoneum.
Procedure: exploratory laparotomy, evacuation of hemoperitoneum, suture hepatorrhaphy.
Anesthesia: general. Allergies: NKDA.
Blood products: 2 units PRBC (started in the trauma bay, completed intraoperatively).
Complications: none apparent. Specimens: none.

Description: Re-entry through the prior midline laparotomy scar. Hemoperitoneum evacuated and the abdomen packed in four quadrants. Packs removed sequentially; the bleeding source was a laceration of the liver, which was controlled with suture hepatorrhaphy. No further bleeding after a period of observation. Spleen, stomach, small bowel and colon run and intact. The prior duodenal repair was inspected and intact. Irrigated. Fascia closed, skin stapled. Hemodynamics normalized after hemorrhage control and transfusion; to the trauma ICU, extubated in the OR.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL TRAUMA CENTER — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admission 01/14/2026. Discharge 01/20/2026.
Received by fax 01/21/2026.

Principal diagnosis: traumatic liver laceration with hemoperitoneum (MVC, restrained driver, airbag deployment).
Operation: 01/14/2026 exploratory laparotomy, suture hepatorrhaphy.
Prior history: laparotomy with duodenal repair 01/2025 after an earlier crash.
Allergies: NKDA.

Course: Hypotensive on arrival with positive FAST, went emergently to the OR as above with 2 units PRBC. Monitored in the trauma ICU through 01/16 with stable hemoglobin and hemodynamics, no further transfusion. Transferred to the surgical floor, diet advanced, ambulating, pain controlled on oral agents. Hemoglobin 10.6 on the morning of discharge. Uncomplicated stay.

Discharge meds:
1. Oxycodone 5 mg every 6 h PRN pain, #15
2. Acetaminophen 1000 mg every 8 h

Activity: no lifting over 10 lb x 6 weeks. No driving on oxycodone.
Follow-up: trauma clinic for staple removal 02/03/2026; PCP within a week, with a CBC.

events.reason: Patient hospitalized after second car accident

documents.title: In the hospital again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted to let you know I was in another car accident Wednesday. They had to operate again, bleeding from my liver this time, and I got blood. Out of the ICU now and on the regular floor. They think I'll go home Monday or Tuesday.

documents.title: RE: In the hospital again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mehmet, I'm so sorry, and glad you're through the worst of it. We'll get the records from the hospital. Once you have a discharge date, let the front desk know and we'll see you within a few days of getting home and recheck your blood count. Text the practice line if anything comes up before then.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 3 days after discharge from the regional trauma center. Records reviewed. Second high-speed crash in a year: belted, airbags out, came in hypotensive with Hgb 9.8 (14.2 here in Dec) and a positive FAST. Emergent laparotomy through his old incision, liver laceration sutured, 2 u PRBC, ICU 2 nights. Discharge Hgb 10.6.

He says he feels "wiped out" but better each day. Pain 4/10, worst with coughing and rolling over. Using oxycodone at night only, acetaminophen during the day. Appetite OK. No fever, no vomiting, no dark stools. Not driving.

Exam: vitals as charted. Tired-appearing but in no distress. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Midline incision stapled, clean, no erythema or drainage. Abdomen soft, tender around the wound only.

A/P
S/p ex lap and hepatorrhaphy for traumatic liver laceration with hemoperitoneum, 1/14/26.
- CBC today.
- Wean off oxycodone, continue acetaminophen.
- Staples out at trauma clinic 2/3. Same 10 lb limit as last year, through late February.
- Recheck CBC in about 6 weeks.
- Talked a bit about how he's doing after two of these; he says he's managing. Knows he can reach me.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your hemoglobin from Friday was 11.4, up from 10.6 when you left the hospital. That's the direction we want. No iron or other treatment needed right now; your body will keep rebuilding. We'll check it again in early March.

documents.title: Trauma Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

Thank you for following Mr. Saleh, whom I saw in trauma clinic on 02/03/2026 after laparotomy and hepatorrhaphy for a liver laceration on 01/14/2026.

He is recovering well. He stopped oxycodone last week and uses acetaminophen occasionally. Eating normally, no fevers. NKDA.

The incision is healing well and the staples were removed today. Abdomen soft with expected tenderness near the wound.

Please continue the 10 lb lifting restriction until six weeks after surgery. I will see him in about five weeks to clear him for full activity.

Sincerely,
Trauma Surgery

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u 7 weeks after hepatorrhaphy. Feels like himself again. Energy back, walking to campus, done with acetaminophen. No abdominal pain, normal appetite and bowels.

Exam: vitals as charted. Color good. Incision healed, no hernia. Abdomen soft, non-tender.

A/P
Recovering from traumatic liver laceration; Hgb today pending at time of note.
- Trauma clinic on Tuesday for clearance.
- Physical in December.

Addendum 3/6 evening: Hgb 13.6, nearly back to his baseline. Messaged him.

documents.title: Trauma Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

Mr. Saleh was seen in trauma clinic on 03/10/2026, eight weeks after laparotomy and hepatorrhaphy. He is asymptomatic and back to his usual routine. His hemoglobin from your office last week was 13.6. NKDA.

The incision is well healed with no hernia, and the abdomen is soft and non-tender.

He has recovered from the liver injury and may return to full activity, including lifting and exercise, without restriction. No further trauma clinic follow-up is planned.

Sincerely,
Trauma Surgery
